Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/5] Existing research has suggested that perceived parenting styles consistently predict academic competence and life satisfaction. Academic competence, which is likely to be of paramount importance in youth from Hong Kong, also has been shown to be related to subjective well-being. In addition, previous studies have hypothesized a general decline in life satisfaction during adolescence attributable to family conflict and school-adjustment problems. However, researchers have yet to examine the relations among maternal parenting style, perceived academic competence, and multiple dimensions of life satisfaction in a longitudinal study.
